children: The latest proposal by the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) seeks to tighten insurance distribution norms by lowering insurers' Expenses of Management (EoM) limits and placing tighter controls on commissions and distributor payouts.

For life insurers, the proposed EoM limit would come down to 15% of premium within two years and 12.5% within five years. For general insurers, the limits would be 25% within two years and 20% within five years, compared with the current 30% limit.

Nomura's assessment of management commentary from Niva Bupa and PB Fintech shows contrasting responses to the proposed changes. Niva Bupa indicated comfort with the EoM cap, while PB Fintech said it would need to rethink its business model.

Niva Bupa, which has a 'Buy' rating from Nomura, indicated "comfort with the newly-proposed EOM (expense of management) cap" during its analyst call on September 24. Management believes that "both commission caps and operating leverage will help them record the 25%-20% EOM cap", proposed to be achieved over the next two and five years, respectively.

In its retail health portfolio, which accounted for 67% of the mix in FY26, management indicated "comfort with agency, direct and even banca channels". In the group business, Niva Bupa is aiming to form new partnerships to offset any pressure from lower volumes.

On customers, management indicated that it would "maintain prices steady for an extended period of time" compared with its current strategy of annual repricing. Nomura said this would be a way of passing on the benefit of lower commissions to end customers and "should help in increasing product demand".

Niva Bupa reiterated mid-teens ROE and a 99% combined insurance service ratio (CISR) by FY29E. The company is likely to revise the timelines to achieve the CISR and will share details after 2Q27F results, Nomura said.

For PB Fintech, which has a 'Neutral' rating from Nomura, management's September 24 concall focused on "the need to bring about changes in its business model". It said it would evolve from a "growth at any cost" mindset to a "rationalised growth" mindset, given the changes to the distribution structure proposed by the regulator.
While PB Fintech has indicated "no mass layoffs or radical reactions", the company plans to trim marketing expenses and slow down hiring.

The company is also evaluating new products, including life insurance savings, credit life and mutual funds, as well as new businesses such as reinsurance broking, reinsurance or insurance manufacturing. PB Fintech is now assigning "higher probability" to becoming an insurance manufacturer.
Separately, management plans to request the regulator to introduce the MGA (managing general agent) format in India, as it believes this can create "responsible distribution" models.

title: IRDAI proposal: Niva Bupa 'Buy' comfortable with EOM cap, PB Fintech 'Neutral' weighs business changes
